stem: How does the analyst start a new dashboard in a workbook?

options.text: Open the Dashboard menu and choose Actions, then Add Action.
options.rationale: Dashboard > Actions defines interactions between sheets that already sit on a dashboard; it does not create one.

options.text: Click the New Story tab and drag the worksheets into the first story point.
options.rationale: That builds a story, a sequence of points, not a dashboard that shows several views at once.

options.text: Click the New Dashboard icon at the bottom of the workbook.
options.rationale: The icon creates an empty dashboard sheet next to the worksheets.

options.text: Right-click a worksheet tab and choose Show Filter for every sheet.
options.rationale: Show Filter adds a filter card to a view; it creates no new sheet.

explanation: A dashboard is its own sheet type. You create it with the New Dashboard icon at the bottom of the workbook and then fill it with views and objects.

stem: Where does the analyst drag a finished view from to place it on a dashboard?

options.text: The Sheets list on the left of the dashboard
options.rationale: The Sheets list holds every worksheet in the workbook, ready to drag onto the dashboard.

options.text: The Data pane, by dragging a field onto the dashboard canvas
options.rationale: Fields belong to worksheets; the dashboard canvas takes sheets and objects, not raw fields.

options.text: The Objects section, by dragging the Horizontal container
options.rationale: The Objects section offers layout containers, text, images and similar items, but not the worksheets themselves.

options.text: The Marks card of the active worksheet, by dragging the Detail button
options.rationale: The Marks card shapes one view; it is not a source of sheets for a dashboard.

explanation: In the dashboard workspace the Sheets list shows the workbook's worksheets. Dragging one into the dashboard on the right adds that view, while the Objects section supplies non-view items.

stem: The head of content wants a title line above the charts on the Viewing at a glance dashboard. Which object fits best?

options.text: Blank
options.rationale: The Blank object only adds empty spacing; it shows no text.

options.text: Navigation
options.rationale: A Navigation object is a button that takes viewers to another sheet, dashboard or story.

options.text: Web Page
options.rationale: A Web Page object displays an external site, not typed text.

options.text: Text
options.rationale: A Text object holds free text such as a dashboard title.

explanation: Text objects carry titles, notes and captions. Blank is for spacing, Navigation for jumping to other sheets, and Web Page for embedding a URL.

stem: A team wants a button on the Overview dashboard that sends viewers to the Regions dashboard. Which object should they add?

options.text: Blank, sized to look like a button
options.rationale: A Blank object is only spacing and has no built-in link to another sheet.

options.text: Navigation
options.rationale: A Navigation object lets viewers move from one dashboard to other sheets, dashboards or stories.

options.text: Image, showing a screenshot of the Regions chart
options.rationale: An Image object displays a picture and does not open another sheet by itself.

options.text: Horizontal, holding the Regions worksheet
options.rationale: A layout container groups objects and does not navigate anywhere.

explanation: Navigation objects exist for exactly this: letting an audience move from one dashboard to other sheets, dashboards or stories.

stem: The analyst needs empty space between two charts so they do not touch. Which Objects item is meant for that?

options.text: Image
options.rationale: An Image object displays a picture, which is more than spacing and needs a file.

options.text: Web Page
options.rationale: A Web Page object loads a URL, so it would show content rather than empty space.

options.text: Navigation
options.rationale: A Navigation object draws a button for jumping to other sheets.

options.text: Blank
options.rationale: The Blank object adds spacing between items.

explanation: Blank is the Objects item for padding and spacing. The other objects carry content such as pictures, pages or navigation buttons.

stem: Driftlight wants its catalogue tool shown live inside a dashboard. Which object embeds that web page?

options.text: Navigation
options.rationale: A Navigation object moves viewers to other sheets, not to external sites.

options.text: Text
options.rationale: A Text object holds typed text, so the page would only appear as a visible link at best.

options.text: Image
options.rationale: An Image object shows a static picture file, not a live page.

options.text: Web Page
options.rationale: A Web Page object embeds the page at a URL on the dashboard.

explanation: The Web Page object embeds a URL in the dashboard. Image shows a static file, Text shows typed text, and Navigation targets sheets, dashboards and stories.

stem: What best describes a dashboard compared with a worksheet?

options.text: It holds one view built from fields on shelves and the Marks card.
options.rationale: That describes a worksheet, where the pills and marks live.

options.text: It is a sequence of story points that each show one sheet with a caption.
options.rationale: That describes a story, which walks the reader through points in order.

options.text: It arranges several worksheets, plus text, images and controls, on one screen.
options.rationale: That is the purpose of a dashboard: compare views side by side and let them interact.

options.text: It stores the data connection and the joins between tables.
options.rationale: Connections and joins belong to the data source, not to a dashboard.

explanation: A worksheet holds a single view. A dashboard combines several of them with objects on one screen, and a story presents sheets or dashboards one point at a time.

stem: Which two items are found in the Objects section of the dashboard workspace? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Horizontal layout container
options.rationale: Horizontal and Vertical containers are Objects items.

options.text: Calculated field
options.rationale: Calculated fields live in the Data pane and are used in worksheets.

options.text: Story point
options.rationale: Story points belong to a story sheet, not to the dashboard Objects list.

options.text: Image
options.rationale: Image is an Objects item for pictures such as a logo.

options.text: Parameter
options.rationale: Parameters are created from the Data pane, not placed as dashboard objects.

explanation: The Objects section includes layout containers, Text, Image, Web Page, Blank and Navigation. Fields, calculations and parameters are worksheet-level concepts.

stem: Which three can the analyst add to a dashboard from the Objects section? (Choose 3 answers.)

options.text: Parameter control card
options.rationale: A parameter control is shown through the parameter, not dragged as an Objects item.

options.text: Text
options.rationale: Text is an Objects item.

options.text: Bin
options.rationale: A bin is a field type made in the Data pane.

options.text: Web Page
options.rationale: Web Page is an Objects item that embeds a URL.

options.text: Marks card
options.rationale: The Marks card is part of a worksheet, not an object.

options.text: Navigation
options.rationale: Navigation is an Objects item for buttons to other sheets.

explanation: Objects such as Text, Web Page and Navigation go on the dashboard from the Objects section. Bins and the Marks card belong to worksheet building.

stem: Which two actions build a dashboard that shows two existing worksheets? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Click the New Story tab
options.rationale: This creates a story, not a dashboard.

options.text: Choose Insert > Sheets in the Tooltip editor
options.rationale: This places a sheet inside a tooltip, not on the dashboard canvas.

options.text: Click the New Dashboard icon
options.rationale: The icon at the bottom of the workbook creates the dashboard sheet.

options.text: Drag the two views from the Sheets list onto the dashboard
options.rationale: Dragging from the Sheets list places each view on the dashboard.

options.text: Open Dashboard > Actions and choose Add Action
options.rationale: Actions connect sheets already placed; they do not place them.

explanation: First create the dashboard with the New Dashboard icon, then drag worksheets from the Sheets list. Actions and tooltips are refinements applied afterwards.

stem: A Navigation object can take viewers to which two kinds of destination? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: A Tableau Prep flow
options.rationale: Navigation objects point to sheets, dashboards and stories, not to Prep flows.

options.text: Another dashboard
options.rationale: Navigation objects can lead to another dashboard.

options.text: A story
options.rationale: Navigation objects can lead to a story.

options.text: The definition of a calculated field
options.rationale: A Navigation object does not open field definitions.

options.text: A parameter's current value
options.rationale: A parameter has a value but is not a destination for navigation.

explanation: Navigation objects let an audience move from one dashboard to other sheets, dashboards or stories.

stem: A Plan filter card is shown on a dashboard with three sheets, and it must filter all three. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Turn on Use as Filter in the corner of the map sheet.
options.rationale: Use as Filter turns selected marks into filters; it does not change which sheets a filter card applies to.

options.text: Open the card menu, choose Apply to Worksheets > Selected Worksheets and click All on dashboard.
options.rationale: This makes the one card filter every sheet on the dashboard.

options.text: Open the card menu, choose Apply to Worksheets > Only This Worksheet.
options.rationale: That limits the filter to the one sheet it was created on, which is the opposite of the goal.

options.text: Add a highlight action from the filter sheet to the other sheets.
options.rationale: A highlight action dims marks instead of filtering them, and it is not a filter card setting.

explanation: The Apply to Worksheets menu on a filter card controls its scope. Choosing Selected Worksheets and then All on dashboard applies it to every sheet on the dashboard.

stem: Viewers should be able to click a bar in the genre chart and have the other sheets on the dashboard filter to that genre, with minimal setup. What is the quickest way?

options.text: Add a Show/Hide button to the genre sheet.
options.rationale: A Show/Hide button folds an object away; it creates no filtering.

options.text: Insert a sheet into the tooltip with Insert > Sheets.
options.rationale: A Viz in Tooltip shows a chart on hover; it does not filter other sheets.

options.text: Choose Only This Worksheet on every filter card.
options.rationale: That restricts filter cards to single sheets and does nothing with clicked marks.

options.text: Enable Use as Filter on the genre sheet.
options.rationale: This turns selected marks into filters for the other sheets on the dashboard in one click.

explanation: Use as Filter is the one-click filter action: selected marks in the sheet filter the other sheets. Custom behaviour is then set in Dashboard > Actions.

stem: Which feature lets viewers type a keyword and make the matching marks stand out while the rest fade?

options.text: Use as Filter on the source sheet
options.rationale: Use as Filter removes non-selected data in other sheets and is not a keyword search.

options.text: Include command buttons in the tooltip
options.rationale: Command buttons give filter and View Data options on hover, not a keyword search.

options.text: Add Show/Hide Button on a container
options.rationale: A Show/Hide button collapses an object and does not highlight marks.

options.text: A data highlighter
options.rationale: A highlighter lets viewers search by keyword or pick from a list; matching marks stand out and the rest fade.

explanation: A data highlighter highlights matching marks and fades the others. It also appears on dashboards and stories once it is added to a worksheet.

stem: Where does the analyst edit the text that appears when a viewer hovers over a mark?

options.text: The Tooltip button on the Marks card
options.rationale: Clicking Tooltip on the Marks card opens the editor for the hover text.

options.text: The Layout pane of the dashboard
options.rationale: The Layout pane sets position, size and title visibility of dashboard items, not tooltip text.

options.text: The Dashboard menu under Actions
options.rationale: Actions define interactions between sheets, not the hover text itself.

options.text: The Analytics pane of the worksheet
options.rationale: The Analytics pane holds items like reference lines, not tooltip text.

explanation: Tooltips are edited per worksheet by selecting Tooltip on the Marks card. The dialog then lets the analyst type text and insert dynamic content.

stem: The analyst edits a tooltip and wants it to show each mark's own Genre, not a fixed word. What should they do?

options.text: Turn on Allow selection by category for the tooltip.
options.rationale: This option selects all marks with the same value; it does not add field values to the text.

options.text: Use the Insert menu at the top of the Tooltip dialog and pick the field.
options.rationale: Insert adds dynamic text such as field values, which change with each mark.

options.text: Type the genre name into the tooltip text once for all marks.
options.rationale: Typed text is static and would read the same on every mark.

options.text: Drag Genre onto the Filters shelf.
options.rationale: A filter limits which data is shown; it does not write the mark's value into a tooltip.

explanation: The Insert menu in the Tooltip editor adds dynamic text, such as field values, so every mark shows its own value.

stem: Driftlight wants a small chart of a genre's top titles to appear when viewers hover a genre bar. How does the analyst set it up?

options.text: On the dashboard, choose Add Show/Hide Button on the bar chart.
options.rationale: A Show/Hide button toggles an object and does not embed a chart in a tooltip.

options.text: In Dashboard > Actions, add a Go to Sheet action that runs on Hover.
options.rationale: Go to Sheet opens another sheet instead of embedding it in a tooltip.

options.text: In the Tooltip editor, choose Insert > Sheets and pick the sheet.
options.rationale: This creates a Viz in Tooltip: a whole sheet is shown inside the tooltip.

options.text: Turn on Include command buttons in the Tooltip dialog.
options.rationale: Command buttons add filter and View Data links; they do not embed a sheet.

explanation: A Viz in Tooltip puts a sheet inside the tooltip, inserted with Insert > Sheets in the Tooltip editor.

stem: A dashboard has a large panel of filter cards that clutters the screen. The analyst wants viewers to fold it away with a button. What should they use?

options.text: Use as Filter on the sheet that holds the panel
options.rationale: Use as Filter converts marks into filters and does not hide objects.

options.text: A data highlighter placed on the panel
options.rationale: A highlighter searches marks and does not fold away objects.

options.text: Add Show/Hide Button from the object's pop-up menu
options.rationale: The pop-up menu in the object's corner offers Add Show/Hide Button to show or hide it.

options.text: Apply to Worksheets > Only This Worksheet on each filter
options.rationale: This changes which sheets a filter affects; it does not hide the panel.

explanation: Show/Hide buttons let viewers collapse and expand an object such as a container of filters. They are added from the pop-up menu in the object's upper corner.

stem: A tooltip should offer viewers links to filter the view and to open View Data without leaving the dashboard. Which tooltip option provides them?

options.text: Include command buttons
options.rationale: Command buttons add filtering options and View Data to the tooltip.

options.text: Allow selection by category
options.rationale: This selects all marks with the same value; it does not add buttons.

options.text: Insert > Sheets
options.rationale: This embeds a sheet in the tooltip rather than adding command buttons.

options.text: Add Show/Hide Button
options.rationale: This belongs to dashboard objects, not to tooltip settings.

explanation: Include command buttons shows filtering and View Data options in the tooltip. Allow selection by category is a separate option that selects marks sharing a value.

stem: Which two statements about tooltip settings are true? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Include command buttons adds filtering and View Data options to the tooltip.
options.rationale: This is what the option provides.

options.text: Include command buttons makes the tooltip open a Go to URL action.
options.rationale: URL actions are defined under Dashboard > Actions.

options.text: Allow selection by category applies a filter to every sheet on the dashboard.
options.rationale: It selects marks; the scope of filtering is set by actions or filter cards.

options.text: Allow selection by category selects all marks with the same value.
options.rationale: This is what the option provides.

options.text: A tooltip can only contain text, never a chart.
options.rationale: A Viz in Tooltip places a whole sheet in the tooltip.

explanation: Both options live in the Tooltip editor: command buttons for filter and View Data options, and category selection for choosing all marks with the same value. Tooltips can also hold a sheet.

stem: Which two are controls a viewer can use directly on a dashboard to explore the data? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: A data highlighter
options.rationale: Viewers search or pick values to make matching marks stand out.

options.text: The Fixed size setting
options.rationale: Size is a layout choice for the author, not a control for exploring data.

options.text: A filter card
options.rationale: Show Filter adds a card the viewer uses to restrict the data.

options.text: The Device Preview button
options.rationale: Device Preview is an authoring tool for layouts.

options.text: The story navigator style
options.rationale: The navigator style belongs to stories, not dashboards.

explanation: Filter cards and highlighters give viewers interactive control. Fixed size, Device Preview and navigator style are authoring and story settings.

stem: Which three are options in the Apply to Worksheets submenu of a filter card? (Choose 3 answers.)

options.text: Selected Worksheets
options.rationale: This opens the list of sheets, with an All on dashboard button.

options.text: Add to Context
options.rationale: Add to Context is on the filter's own menu and changes when it runs, not which sheets it applies to.

options.text: All Using This Data Source
options.rationale: The filter applies to every sheet that uses the same data source.

options.text: Use as Filter
options.rationale: Use as Filter is in the upper corner of a sheet on the dashboard, not in the filter card's menu.

options.text: Only This Worksheet
options.rationale: This keeps the filter local to the current sheet.

options.text: Add Show/Hide Button
options.rationale: Show/Hide buttons come from an object's pop-up menu and fold the object away.

explanation: The submenu offers Selected Worksheets, All Using Related Data Sources, All Using This Data Source and Only This Worksheet.

stem: On a dashboard, clicking a country on the map should dim the other values in the line chart instead of removing them. Which action type fits?

options.text: Highlight
options.rationale: A highlight action keeps all marks and dims those that do not match.

options.text: Filter
options.rationale: A filter action removes marks that do not match from the target sheets.

options.text: Go to Sheet
options.rationale: Go to Sheet opens another sheet; it neither filters nor highlights.

options.text: Change Set Values
options.rationale: This changes the members of a set and does not dim marks on its own.

explanation: Filter actions remove non-matching marks, while highlight actions keep every mark and dim the rest. When other values must stay visible, use highlight.

stem: From which menu does the analyst add a filter action to a dashboard?

options.text: The Tooltip dialog on the Marks card
options.rationale: The Tooltip dialog edits hover text and has no action list.

options.text: Dashboard > Actions, then Add Action
options.rationale: This is where actions of every type are created and edited.

options.text: The Layout pane
options.rationale: The Layout pane sets item position and size.

options.text: The Analytics pane
options.rationale: The Analytics pane holds items like reference lines.

explanation: Dashboard > Actions lists a dashboard's actions; Add Action lets the analyst choose a type such as Filter or Highlight.

stem: Which Run action on setting fires an action as soon as the viewer moves the pointer over a mark, without clicking?

options.text: Select
options.rationale: Select needs the viewer to click a mark.

options.text: Hover
options.rationale: Hover triggers the action when the pointer is over a mark.

options.text: Menu
options.rationale: Menu puts a link in the tooltip that the viewer must click.

options.text: Show all values
options.rationale: This controls what happens when a filter selection is cleared; it is not a trigger.

explanation: Run action on offers Hover, Select and Menu. Hover reacts to the pointer, Select to a click and Menu to a link in the tooltip.

stem: A filter action runs from the map. When the viewer clears the selection, the other sheets should show all members again. Which setting is needed?

options.text: Leave the filter
options.rationale: The sheets would stay filtered to the last selection.

options.text: Exclude all values
options.rationale: The target sheets would show no marks.

options.text: Show all values
options.rationale: This restores every member in the target sheets when the selection is cleared.

options.text: Keep current value
options.rationale: This setting belongs to parameter actions and does not apply to a filter action.

explanation: A filter action offers Leave the filter, Show all values or Exclude all values when the selection is cleared. Keep current value is for parameter actions.

stem: Which two are choices for what a filter action does when the selection is cleared? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Keep current value
options.rationale: This option is offered by parameter actions.

options.text: Leave the filter
options.rationale: The target sheets keep the previous filter.

options.text: Set value to
options.rationale: This option is offered by parameter actions.

options.text: Run action on Menu
options.rationale: That decides how the action starts, not what happens on clearing.

options.text: Exclude all values
options.rationale: The target sheets show no marks.

explanation: For filter actions the clear-selection choices are Leave the filter, Show all values and Exclude all values. Parameter actions have their own pair of options.

stem: Which text in a Go to URL action inserts the value of the Title ID field into the link?

options.text: `https://example.com/title?id=[Title ID]`
options.rationale: Square brackets reference a field inside a calculated field, not in a URL action.

options.text: `https://example.com/title?id={Title ID}`
options.rationale: Curly braces belong to level of detail expressions and are not read as field placeholders in a URL.

options.text: `https://example.com/title?id=<Title ID>`
options.rationale: Field names go in angle brackets, and Tableau replaces the placeholder with the selected mark's value.

options.text: `https://example.com/title?id=(Title ID)`
options.rationale: Parentheses are plain text in a URL, so the link would contain the words "Title ID" literally.

explanation: In a Go to URL action the URL may contain field names in angle brackets. When the viewer acts on a mark, Tableau substitutes that mark's value into the link.

stem: A Go to URL action uses `<Subscriber ID>`, but the link comes out without the ID because the source worksheet does not show that field. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Put `Subscriber ID` on Detail on the source sheet's Marks card.
options.rationale: A field used in a URL action must be in the view, and Detail is enough without changing the chart's look.

options.text: Create a Change Parameter action that stores the ID in a parameter.
options.rationale: A parameter action sets a parameter value; it does not make a field available to a URL action.

options.text: Add a filter card for `Subscriber ID` to the dashboard.
options.rationale: A filter card limits which marks are shown but does not add the field to the view's marks.

options.text: Switch the action to Run action on Menu instead of Select.
options.rationale: How the action is triggered has no effect on which fields the URL can read.

explanation: URL actions can only insert fields that are used in the source view. Placing the field on Detail makes it available without altering what the chart displays.

stem: Clicking a country mark on the overview dashboard should open the separate Regions dashboard. Which type of action does that?

options.text: Filter, with the Regions dashboard as the target sheet
options.rationale: A filter action restricts data in sheets that appear on the same dashboard; it does not open another sheet.

options.text: Highlight, with the Regions dashboard as the target sheet
options.rationale: Highlight dims marks in target views and does not navigate anywhere.

options.text: Change Set Values, so the set points to the Regions dashboard
options.rationale: Change Set Values changes the members of a set; sets are not navigation targets.

options.text: Go to Sheet, with the Regions dashboard as the target
options.rationale: Go to Sheet opens another sheet, dashboard or story when the viewer acts on a mark.

explanation: Go to Sheet is the action type for navigating from a mark to a different sheet, dashboard or story. Filter and highlight actions affect the views already on screen.

stem: Viewers should click a genre bar and have a parameter take that genre as its value, which then drives a calculation elsewhere. Which action type fits?

options.text: Go to URL, with the genre in angle brackets
options.rationale: Go to URL opens a web page and never writes into a parameter.

options.text: Change Parameter, with the genre field as the source field
options.rationale: A parameter action sets a parameter to the value of the selected mark.

options.text: Filter, with the calculation's sheet as the target
options.rationale: A filter action removes marks from target sheets and does not set a parameter.

options.text: Highlight, with the genre field as the field to match
options.rationale: Highlight fades non-matching marks and does not change any parameter.

explanation: Change Parameter actions pass the selected mark's value into a parameter. Calculations or reference lines that use that parameter then update when the viewer clicks.

stem: Which two are possible targets of a Go to URL action? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: A new browser tab
options.rationale: The URL can open in the viewer's browser in a new tab.

options.text: A Filter action on another sheet
options.rationale: A filter action is its own action type and not a destination for a link.

options.text: A story point of the same workbook
options.rationale: Opening a sheet, dashboard or story is the job of a Go to Sheet action, not of a URL action.

options.text: A Web Page object on the same dashboard
options.rationale: The URL can load inside a Web Page object that sits on the dashboard.

options.text: A Show/Hide button next to the source sheet
options.rationale: Show/Hide buttons fold objects away; they are not link targets.

explanation: A URL action either opens the address in a browser tab or loads it into a Web Page object on the dashboard. Navigating to other workbook sheets is handled by Go to Sheet.

stem: Which two are action types in the Dashboard > Actions dialog? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Apply to Worksheets
options.rationale: This is a submenu of a filter card, not an action type.

options.text: Change Set Values
options.rationale: The action changes the members of a set when the viewer selects marks.

options.text: Add Show/Hide Button
options.rationale: This is a menu entry on a dashboard object, not an action type.

options.text: Include command buttons
options.rationale: This is a tooltip setting, not an action type.

options.text: Go to Sheet
options.rationale: The action opens another sheet, dashboard or story.

explanation: The Actions dialog offers Filter, Highlight, Go to URL, Go to Sheet, Change Parameter and Change Set Values. Items such as Apply to Worksheets and Show/Hide buttons are separate dashboard features.

stem: Which description matches tiled items on a dashboard?

options.text: They float above other objects and can be placed at any pixel position.
options.rationale: That describes floating items, which can be layered over other objects.

options.text: They do not overlap and become part of a single-layer grid.
options.rationale: Tiled items share one non-overlapping grid, so adding one resizes its neighbours.

options.text: They are always inside a vertical layout container and resize only in height.
options.rationale: Tiled items need not be in a container, and containers can be horizontal or vertical.

options.text: They keep a fixed pixel size when the dashboard is resized.
options.rationale: Size is set per dashboard (Fixed, Range, Automatic), not by tiling.

explanation: Tiled is the default way to place objects: a single layer without overlap. Floating is the alternative when objects must be layered.

stem: The analyst drags a legend onto the dashboard and wants it to sit on top of a map in the corner. What should they hold while dragging?

options.text: Ctrl, to copy the legend onto the map
options.rationale: Ctrl-dragging does not turn an item into a floating one.

options.text: Alt, to attach the legend to the map's layout container
options.rationale: Alt is not how an item is made to float or to join a container.

options.text: Tab, to toggle between Tiled and Floating
options.rationale: Tab is not a layout modifier on the dashboard.

options.text: Shift, to make the item float
options.rationale: Holding Shift while dragging places the item as a floating object that can overlap others.

explanation: Floating items are layered over other objects. Hold Shift while dragging to float an item, and use it sparingly, for things like legends or a logo.

stem: Three sheets should stack top to bottom and share the dashboard's height evenly as the dashboard is resized. Which container fits?

options.text: A vertical layout container
options.rationale: A vertical container adjusts the height of the views and objects it holds.

options.text: A horizontal layout container
options.rationale: A horizontal container resizes the width of its contents, so it lines items up side by side.

options.text: A Blank object
options.rationale: Blank adds empty space; it does not organise sheets.

options.text: A Navigation object
options.rationale: Navigation creates a button to go to another sheet, not a layout.

explanation: Horizontal containers resize the width of what they contain and vertical containers adjust height. Containers keep groups of sheets aligned when the dashboard changes size.

stem: Which dashboard size setting is the default for a new dashboard?

options.text: Automatic, which fills the window
options.rationale: Automatic adapts to the window but is not the default.

options.text: Range, between a minimum and a maximum
options.rationale: Range is chosen deliberately to allow a limited amount of resizing.

options.text: Fixed size
options.rationale: Fixed size is the default, and a preset such as Desktop Browser can be picked.

options.text: Fit width, as recommended for phones
options.rationale: Fit width is an option for device layouts, not the dashboard's default size.

explanation: A new dashboard has a fixed size, so it looks the same everywhere. Range and Automatic let it adapt to the viewer's window instead.

stem: A dashboard should always fill whatever browser window it is opened in, even if views are squeezed. Which size setting does that?

options.text: Automatic
options.rationale: Automatic resizes the dashboard to fill the window.

options.text: Fixed size with the Desktop Browser preset
options.rationale: A fixed size stays the same regardless of the window.

options.text: Range with a minimum and a maximum
options.rationale: Range resizes only between its limits, so it does not always fill the window.

options.text: Floating layout for every object
options.rationale: Floating changes how objects are placed, not the overall dashboard size.

explanation: Automatic fills the window and adapts to it, at the risk of squeezing views. Fixed and Range limit the amount of adaptation.

stem: Where does the analyst type the exact x and y position, in pixels, for a floating object?

options.text: The Size section of the Dashboard pane
options.rationale: That section sets the size of the whole dashboard, not an item's position.

options.text: The Marks card of the source sheet
options.rationale: The Marks card shapes marks in one worksheet.

options.text: The Dashboard > Actions dialog
options.rationale: Actions define interactions and have no position settings.

options.text: The Layout pane
options.rationale: The Layout pane sets an item's position and size, and whether its title shows.

explanation: For fine control, select the item and use the Layout pane. It shows the item's position and size in pixels as well as its title setting.

stem: The analyst wants a separate arrangement of the dashboard for tablets. How do they start?

options.text: Duplicate the dashboard and rename it for tablets.
options.rationale: This works but makes two dashboards, and device layouts are meant to keep one dashboard with several layouts.

options.text: Click Device Preview, pick the device type, then click Add Layout.
options.rationale: Device Preview shows device frames, and Add Layout (for example Add Tablet Layout) creates the device-specific layout.

options.text: Set the dashboard size to Range and enter tablet dimensions.
options.rationale: Range allows resizing between limits and does not create a tablet layout.

options.text: Add a Navigation object that sends tablet viewers to another sheet.
options.rationale: Navigation buttons are chosen by the viewer, not by device.

explanation: Device-specific layouts live inside a single dashboard. Open Device Preview, select the device and add the layout; it then appears under Default on the Dashboard tab.

stem: How does the analyst begin a story in a workbook?

options.text: Click the New Dashboard icon and enable the story option.
options.rationale: New Dashboard creates a dashboard; the sheet type for stories is separate.

options.text: Choose Dashboard > Actions and add a Go to Sheet action.
options.rationale: A Go to Sheet action navigates from marks and does not create a story.

options.text: Click the New Story tab.
options.rationale: This opens a story sheet where story points can be added.

options.text: Open Device Preview and click Add Layout.
options.rationale: Device layouts belong to dashboards.

explanation: A story is its own sheet type. It is created with the New Story tab and then filled with story points.

stem: The analyst has dragged a dashboard into the first story point. How do they add a one-line summary of the point?

options.text: Click Add a caption on the story point and type it.
options.rationale: Each story point can carry a caption that summarises it.

options.text: Edit the dashboard's title in the Layout pane.
options.rationale: That changes the dashboard object's own title and not the story point's caption.

options.text: Add a Text object from the dashboard Objects section.
options.rationale: That puts text inside the dashboard rather than writing the caption of the story point.

options.text: Edit the tooltip on the Marks card.
options.rationale: Tooltips appear on hover over marks and are not story captions.

explanation: Story points have a caption box above the content where the analyst writes a short summary of what the point shows.

stem: The analyst wants a second story point that starts as a copy of the current one so that they can change only a filter. Which command suits that?

options.text: Blank
options.rationale: Blank adds an empty point with no content, so the sheet would have to be added again.

options.text: Update
options.rationale: Update overwrites the current point's saved state and does not add a point.

options.text: Add Show/Hide Button
options.rationale: Show/Hide buttons belong to dashboard objects.

options.text: Duplicate
options.rationale: Duplicate copies the current story point so it can then be adjusted (filter, highlight).

explanation: To add a point, choose Blank for a fresh one or Duplicate to copy the current one. Duplicating is quickest when the next point differs only slightly.

stem: In a story point, the analyst filters the dashboard to one region. How do they keep that state in the point?

options.text: Click Save as New on the Story pane.
options.rationale: Save as New keeps both versions, so the original point would stay as it was.

options.text: Click Update on the story toolbar above the navigator box.
options.rationale: Update saves the changed sheet state back into the current story point.

options.text: Select Dashboard > Actions and add a filter action.
options.rationale: An action is a dashboard interaction and does not store state in a story point.

options.text: Switch the dashboard to Fixed size.
options.rationale: Dashboard size has no connection to what is remembered in a story point.

explanation: After changing the sheet inside a point, Update stores the new state in that point. A story point remembers filters and selections as saved.

stem: After changing a story point's filter, the analyst wants to keep the old version of the point and also have the changed one. What should they do?

options.text: Click Update on the story toolbar.
options.rationale: Update replaces the saved state, so the old version would be lost.

options.text: Click Blank and rebuild the point.
options.rationale: Blank adds an empty point and would need the whole sheet to be added again.

options.text: Click Save as New.
options.rationale: Save as New stores the change as a new point and leaves the original in place.

options.text: Add a data highlighter to the story point.
options.rationale: A highlighter only helps viewers find marks and does not save versions of a point.

explanation: Update overwrites the current point, whereas Save as New keeps both versions side by side.

stem: Where does the analyst choose the navigator style of a story and show or hide the next and previous arrows?

options.text: In the Story pane
options.rationale: The Story pane controls how viewers navigate the story, such as navigator style and arrows.

options.text: In the Layout pane
options.rationale: The Layout pane sets item position, size and title for dashboard objects.

options.text: In the Tooltip editor
options.rationale: The Tooltip editor sets the text shown on hover over marks.

options.text: In the Dashboard > Actions dialog
options.rationale: Actions define interactions between sheets and do not control story navigation.

explanation: The Story pane lets the analyst pick a navigator style and show or hide the arrows.

stem: How does a story differ from a dashboard?

options.text: A story shows several worksheets at once; a dashboard shows them one after another.
options.rationale: This reverses the two: a dashboard shows several sheets at the same time.

options.text: A story can only contain worksheets, but a dashboard can contain dashboards.
options.rationale: A story point can show either a worksheet or a dashboard.

options.text: A story is for editing; a dashboard is for viewing only.
options.rationale: Both can be viewed and edited; they differ in structure.

options.text: A story is a sequence of points, each showing one sheet or dashboard with a caption.
options.rationale: Points are visited in order, so a story walks the reader through an argument.

explanation: A dashboard arranges several sheets on one screen. A story is a series of story points, each showing one sheet or dashboard, often with a caption.

stem: Which two are layout containers in the Objects section? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Horizontal
options.rationale: A horizontal layout container resizes the width of the items it holds.

options.text: Blank
options.rationale: Blank adds empty space between objects; it does not group them.

options.text: Navigation
options.rationale: Navigation creates buttons that take viewers to other sheets.

options.text: Vertical
options.rationale: A vertical layout container adjusts the height of the items it holds.

options.text: Web Page
options.rationale: Web Page embeds a page by URL and is not a container.

explanation: Horizontal and vertical layout containers group views and objects so they stay aligned when the dashboard resizes.

stem: Which two statements about device-specific layouts are true? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: They require a separate workbook for every device type.
options.rationale: One dashboard can carry layouts for desktop, tablet and phone.

options.text: A phone layout can be generated automatically with Auto-Generate Layout.
options.rationale: Tableau can build a phone layout from the default one automatically.

options.text: They are defined in the Dashboard > Actions dialog.
options.rationale: Device layouts are added in Device Preview, not in actions.

options.text: Fit width is a recommended size option for phone layouts.
options.rationale: Fit width is recommended for phones.

options.text: They only work if Show sheets as tabs is selected on publishing.
options.rationale: The help says to clear Show sheets as tabs so the device layouts are used.

explanation: A dashboard can hold device layouts for desktop, tablet and phone. A phone layout can be auto-generated and works best with Fit width.

stem: Which three are size settings for a dashboard? (Choose 3 answers.)

options.text: Fixed size
options.rationale: A fixed size looks the same everywhere and is the default.

options.text: Fit width
options.rationale: Fit width is an option for device layouts rather than a dashboard-wide size setting.

options.text: Range
options.rationale: Range sets a minimum and a maximum size.

options.text: Entire View
options.rationale: Entire View fits a worksheet in its window; it is not a dashboard size setting.

options.text: Automatic
options.rationale: Automatic fills the available window.

explanation: A dashboard's size is Fixed size (the default), Range or Automatic. Fit width and Entire View belong to other contexts.

stem: Which two items are the typical use of floating objects? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: The main grid of three charts
options.rationale: The main charts normally sit tiled in a grid so that they never overlap.

options.text: A title row across the top of every dashboard
options.rationale: A title is normally tiled in a row of the layout.

options.text: A legend placed in a corner of a chart
options.rationale: Legends are a typical floating item because they sit over other content.

options.text: A vertical container for stacked sheets
options.rationale: Containers are normally tiled to keep sheets aligned.

options.text: A company logo in a corner
options.rationale: A logo is a typical floating item layered above the layout.

explanation: Floating items can be layered over other objects, so use them sparingly, for things such as legends or a logo, and tile the main content.

stem: Which two can the analyst show in a story point? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: A single field dragged from the Data pane
options.rationale: Fields are used in worksheets; a story point shows a sheet or dashboard.

options.text: A worksheet
options.rationale: A story point can show a worksheet.

options.text: A dashboard
options.rationale: A story point can show a dashboard.

options.text: A parameter
options.rationale: Parameters drive calculations and are not shown as points.

options.text: A Navigation object by itself
options.rationale: Navigation objects sit on dashboards and do not form a story point.

explanation: Each story point shows one sheet or dashboard. The point also remembers the state of that sheet, such as filters.

stem: Which two statements about story points are true? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: A story point remembers the state of its sheet, such as filters and selections.
options.rationale: The same dashboard can appear in several points, each with a different state.

options.text: A filter change in a point is saved automatically without clicking Update.
options.rationale: The analyst saves the change by clicking Update or Save as New.

options.text: A story can contain only one dashboard.
options.rationale: The same or different sheets and dashboards can appear in any number of points.

options.text: A caption can summarise each story point.
options.rationale: Click Add a caption to summarise the point.

options.text: Story points are ordered by the dashboard's size setting.
options.rationale: Order comes from the sequence in the story, not from dashboard size.

explanation: A story point stores its sheet's state and may have a caption. Changes are saved with Update or Save as New.

stem: Which three commands create or save a story point in the story toolbar? (Choose 3 answers.)

options.text: Blank
options.rationale: Blank adds an empty point.

options.text: Duplicate
options.rationale: Duplicate copies the current point as a new one.

options.text: Add Show/Hide Button
options.rationale: This is a dashboard-object command and not a story-point command.

options.text: Save as New
options.rationale: Save as New stores the changed point as a new one.

options.text: Add Layout
options.rationale: Add Layout creates device layouts for a dashboard.

explanation: A new point comes from Blank, Duplicate or Save as New; Update replaces the current point's state. Dashboard-object and device-layout commands are separate.
